title: Phlix Hub settings
description: Schema describing the editable settings for the Phlix Hub. The hub is the identity and directory service for a Phlix estate: it enrolls servers, mints and renews the JWTs those servers authenticate with, brokers the reverse-tunnel relay, and owns cross-server federation and sharing. It does NOT scan libraries or transcode media — that is the server's job. Property keys are the literal dotted setting keys and MUST match Phlix\Hub\Hub\HubSettingsRepository::ALLOWED_KEYS, which is the writable allow-list the hub settings controller enumerates; the schema supplies only the render metadata for those keys. Each key is a dotted path into phlix-hub/config/<file>.php (first segment = flat config file name) and must resolve to a non-null default. Boot-bound infrastructure and secrets — the hub JWT secret, relay TLS material, the hub base/public domain baked into issued enrollment JWTs, ACME/TLS provisioning toggles, host/port/worker counts, and Sonarr/Radarr API keys — are deliberately excluded and are enumerated in HubSettingsRepository::DENIED_KEYS. Numeric `minimum`/`maximum`/`default` literals are written with the exact JSON lexical form the hub settings API has always served for that key (the hub projects them verbatim — `60.0` stays a float, `0` stays an int), so upgrading the hub's meta source never moves a wire byte.

server.enrollment_ttl.description: How long a server enrollment token remains valid after being issued, in seconds.
server.enrollment_ttl.label: Enrollment token TTL
server.enrollment_ttl.helpText: When a server enrolls with this hub it receives a signed JSON Web Token valid for this many seconds; after that it must renew. The shipped value is 604800 seconds (7 days). Longer values mean fewer renewal round-trips but widen the window in which a leaked enrollment token could be replayed. The value is read each time a token is minted, so a change applies to the next enrollment without a restart — tokens already issued keep the lifetime they were minted with.

auth.access_ttl.description: Hub JWT access-token lifetime in seconds.
auth.access_ttl.label: Access token TTL
auth.access_ttl.helpText: How many seconds a hub access token stays valid before the client must exchange its refresh token for a new one. Shorter lifetimes shrink the damage window of a stolen token at the cost of more refresh calls. The shipped value is 3600 seconds (1 hour). The value is resolved on every token mint, so a change applies to newly issued tokens immediately; tokens already in circulation keep their original expiry.

auth.refresh_ttl.label: Refresh token TTL
auth.refresh_ttl.helpText: The maximum age of a refresh token before it can no longer be exchanged for a new access token and the user must sign in again. This should be substantially longer than the access token TTL. The shipped value is 604800 seconds (7 days). The value is resolved on every token mint, so a change applies to newly issued tokens immediately.

auth.signups_disabled.description: Close self-service user signups on this hub.
auth.signups_disabled.label: Disable new signups
auth.signups_disabled.helpText: When true, the hub's registration endpoint rejects every new signup with 403 auth.signups_disabled before credentials are even checked; existing users keep signing in normally. The shipped default is false (signups open, mirroring the boot-time HUB_SIGNUPS_ENABLED environment flag which defaults to true). The gate consults the effective value per signup through the hub settings resolver, so a change applies live without a restart; if the settings read fails the hub degrades to the boot-time flag.

hub.maintenance_mode.description: Gate all hub API traffic behind a 503 maintenance response.
hub.maintenance_mode.label: Maintenance mode
hub.maintenance_mode.helpText: When enabled, the hub answers 503 provider_unavailable for API traffic. Auth, hub-settings, admin settings/restart and /health stay reachable so the off-switch is never locked behind the gate; the /app SPA shell keeps serving. Live within ~1s per worker; a settings outage fails OPEN to the HUB_MAINTENANCE_MODE boot flag.

federation.enabled.description: Master switch for hub-to-hub federation traffic.
federation.enabled.label: Enable hub federation
federation.enabled.helpText: Master switch for hub-to-hub federation. Off: peer mutations 409 provider.not_configured, inbound handshake/DATA frames are refused or dropped, and outbound dials stop. Reads and hub-config CRUD stay open; the :8805 listener stays bound until a restart. Re-enabling instantly re-admits traffic on links that survived the off-window, and re-establishes links that dropped while off within <=60s automatically (the reconnect chain parks at the <=60s backoff cap during the disabled window and re-checks on that cadence — no restart or explicit trigger needed). The same cap also throttles the disabled-window re-check cadence; a hub-config save / peer relay toggle still dials immediately.

requests.auto_approve.description: Approve newly filed media requests immediately, best effort.
requests.auto_approve.label: Auto-approve media requests
requests.auto_approve.helpText: Newly filed requests are approved immediately after the pending row lands (best-effort: any approval failure — arr disabled, down, quota — leaves the request pending exactly like the manual queue). Live per create.

invite.default_expiry_seconds.description: Invite lifetime applied when the creator omits an explicit expiry.
invite.default_expiry_seconds.label: Default invite expiry (seconds)
invite.default_expiry_seconds.helpText: Invite lifetime applied ONLY when the creator omits expires_in (an explicit body value always wins). 0 = never expire; 604800 = the 7-day default invites shipped with before this setting. Live per create.

server.max_servers_per_user.description: Per-account cap on owned servers; 0 means unlimited.
server.max_servers_per_user.label: Max servers per user
server.max_servers_per_user.helpText: Per-account server quota checked at claim time against ALL owned servers (any status). 0 = unlimited, the shipped behavior. Rare concurrent claims of DIFFERENT codes may overshoot by the concurrency count — a quota guard, not a billing-strict invariant.

server.max_users_per_server.description: Cap on distinct active collaborator users per server; 0 means unlimited.
server.max_users_per_server.label: Max collaborators per server
server.max_users_per_server.helpText: Distinct active collaborator users per server, enforced on share create and invite redeem. 0 = unlimited, the shipped behavior. Returning collaborators (reactivation, or already active on another library of the same server) never count as new.

server.metrics.enabled.description: Arm per-worker metrics collection for relay and HTTP workers.
server.metrics.enabled.label: Enable metrics collection
server.metrics.enabled.helpText: Read once per worker at boot (HTTP/relay workers arm their collectors in onWorkerStart); mid-lifetime flips apply to NEW workers — use the graceful restart to recycle. Metrics flush/prune stop when every worker boots with this off.

server.metrics.retention_days.description: Days of server metrics rollups and connection rows to keep.
server.metrics.retention_days.label: Metrics retention (days)
server.metrics.retention_days.helpText: Rollup/connections older than this are pruned on the relay worker flush ticks. Live: re-read every prune, so shrinking the window deletes within one tick. Clamped 1..3650 at read.

server.relay.reconnect_drain_grace_secon.description: Grace window for a displaced relay tunnel to finish in-flight requests.
server.relay.reconnect_drain_grace_secon.label: Reconnect drain grace (seconds)
server.relay.reconnect_drain_grace_secon.helpText: Seconds a displaced incumbent tunnel keeps draining in-flight requests after a validated reconnect. 0 = immediate hard displacement. Live at each displacement event; clamped 0..300 at read.

server.rate_limit.description: Sparse JSON overrides merged over the hub's static rate-limiter section.
server.rate_limit.label: Rate-limit overrides (JSON)
server.rate_limit.helpText: Sparse override blob over config/server.php rate_limit, e.g. {"login":{"max":10},"cap":5000}. Known surface keys: login, proxy, heartbeat, jwks, relay_connect, client_mount, mcp, alexa, signup, cap. Values must be integers > 0 to count; unknown keys are ignored. Applied per worker at boot — use the graceful restart to recycle. Tightening signup/login limits while locked out is not possible: limits exist to protect the hub, and the exempt maintenance paths do not bypass them.

server.arr.sonarr.enabled.description: Enable the Sonarr integration for request approval.
server.arr.sonarr.enabled.label: Sonarr integration enabled
server.arr.sonarr.enabled.helpText: Overrides HUB_SONARR_ENABLED live at each approval. The API key stays env-only (HUB_SONARR_API_KEY) and is never exposed through the settings surface — see the DENIED_KEYS admission law.

server.arr.sonarr.url.description: Base URL of the Sonarr instance approvals are sent to.
server.arr.sonarr.url.label: Sonarr base URL
server.arr.sonarr.url.helpText: Live at each approval. Admin-trust boundary: this URL is fetched server-side from the settings write surface (same trust class as other admin-controlled URLs); api_key never leaves the env.

server.arr.radarr.enabled.description: Enable the Radarr integration for request approval.
server.arr.radarr.enabled.label: Radarr integration enabled
server.arr.radarr.enabled.helpText: Overrides HUB_RADARR_ENABLED live at each approval. The API key stays env-only (HUB_RADARR_API_KEY) and is never exposed through the settings surface — see the DENIED_KEYS admission law.

server.arr.radarr.url.description: Base URL of the Radarr instance approvals are sent to.
server.arr.radarr.url.label: Radarr base URL
server.arr.radarr.url.helpText: Live at each approval. Admin-trust boundary: this URL is fetched server-side from the settings write surface (same trust class as other admin-controlled URLs); api_key never leaves the env.
